header:
Date: 2027-11-29
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Recording: yes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samira Rao (Redwood SE), Luca Marin (Redwood Solutions Eng), Dr. Neha Patel (Oxbridge ML Eng), Maya Ortiz (Oxbridge Product), Jonas Ek (Oxbridge Infra), Priya Shah (Oxbridge SRE)
summary: Mid-pilot weekly sync to review latency and throughput snapshots vs the incumbent baseline. Oxbridge reported p95 latency delta narrowing after routing and quantization changes; Redwood proposed dedicated slot test and follow-up deep-dive. Action items and next steps agreed.
topics: Bench numbers (p50/p95), sequence length distribution, batching strategy, KV/prefix cache behavior, quantization accuracy tradeoffs, dedicated slot vs hosted routing, unit token cost, SLA targets
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call, uh, we have about 50 minutes, good to go?
[00:12] Dr. Neha Patel: Yep, Neha here, Maya, Jonas and Priya on my side, thanks.
[00:20] Samira Rao: Samira from Redwood, I'll lead the perf recap and then we'll triage.
[00:28] Maya Ortiz: Hi all.
[00:33] Alex Chen: Cool. Quick agenda: 1) bench snapshot vs your baseline provider runs, 2) what changed since last week (routing tweak + quant), 3) recommended dedicated-slot test, 4) next steps.
[00:50] Jonas Ek: Quick note - we pushed an updated traffic mix yesterday, so most sequences are longer, average 1.6k tokens, not the 800 we originally thought, so that changed throughput numbers.
[01:05] Samira Rao: Right and that's visible in the spreadsheet - thanks for flagging. The p95 we saw on your baseline was 420ms for short seqs but with longer seqs that p95 moves to 1.1s. Our Redwood default routing without prefix cache had p95 1.3s but after enabling KV cache and a smaller batch target it moved to 780ms.
[01:33] Dr. Neha Patel: There was also a mis-match on batching - the incumbent was doing micro-batching per connection, we had a bug in our client that disabled keep-alive so we weren't getting packing. That's fixed now.
[01:48] Alex Chen: Good call. So the headline: delta to baseline p95 is now approx +60ms for most traffic slices, which is much better than the +300ms we saw two weeks back.
[02:03] Maya Ortiz: Can you share the exact run IDs? We want the raw logs to correlate with our tracing.
[02:10] Alex Chen: Yes - I'll upload annotated bench spreadsheet with run IDs and raw traces link. (link: drive.redwood/oxbridge/bench-annotated)
[02:18] Priya Shah: On unit cost, rough calc from your sheet shows Redwood unit token cost about 15% lower once we apply quantize-8 and the smarter batching suggestion, is that right?
[02:29] Samira Rao: Roughly yes — assuming 8-bit quantization with negligible quality delta. But note quality checks are still pending, Neha, you are running the prompt regression?
[02:40] Dr. Neha Patel: We're running regression now on 5000 prompts, early signs are ok but a few longer-context hallucination cases popped up when quantized aggressively.
[02:52] Samira Rao: That's expected, we can dial quantize to 6-bit mixed or use dynamic quant profile for tokens after 1k to preserve fidelity.
[03:04] Alex Chen: On routing: last week we switched policy to latency-first for the pilot slice; that caused more small batches but lower tail lat — Samira, correct me if im wrong.
[03:15] Samira Rao: Yeah, latency-first pushes requests to smallest capacity nodes, reduces queueing but you lose some batching efficiency. We experimented with a hybrid policy: latency for <512 tokens, cost for >512 which improved throughput for long sequences.
[03:33] Jonas Ek: The hybrid sounds promising. What's the throughput delta numbers?
[03:37] Samira Rao: For the long-seq traffic, throughput (tokens/s) rose from 4.2k to 6.8k when we allowed cost-aware routing and slightly larger batch windows; p50 improved from 220ms to 150ms and p95 from 1.3s to 780ms.
[03:52] Dr. Neha Patel: How reproducible are those numbers — is that from a single-run or aggregated?
[03:58] Samira Rao: Aggregated across four 30-minute runs with different seeds; I'll mark the runs in the spreadsheet.
[04:06] Maya Ortiz: There's a line in your sheet that says 'fallback to smaller variant' — can you explain what that is?
[04:11] Samira Rao: Sure: when queueing exceeds threshold we fall back from the full fp16 model to a quantized variant that's latency-optimized. That avoids timeouts but can increase error on some prompts.
[04:22] Alex Chen: Oxbridge had asked about worst-case p99 — we measured p99 at 2.1s on the long traffic slice during peak. Baseline provider had p99 of 1.9s on their config.
[04:36] Priya Shah: We need p99 under 2s to meet our internal SLA for production.
[04:41] Samira Rao: We can get under 2s with a dedicated slot and tuned batcher plus warm KV cache. The dedicated slot reduces cross-tenant noise and enables reserved GPU packing.
[04:52] Dr. Neha Patel: Can you quantify the dedicated slot improvement?
[04:55] Samira Rao: Early estimate: p95 drops by ~20-30% and p99 by ~10-15% for your long-seq traffic when moving to dedicated — because we eliminate tail noise from other tenants and control scheduling windows. We'll validate with a 2-hour dedicated run.
[05:14] Jonas Ek: For the dedicated run, what GPU types will you use? We want parity with baseline which uses A100 80GB.
[05:20] Samira Rao: We can provision NVL 80 or equivalent; for parity testing we'll do A100p or the customer's requested instance. I'll note that in the test plan.
[05:31] Alex Chen: Also note memory pressure with 8k contexts if you keep fp16. Quantization reduces mem and helps batching.
[05:37] Dr. Neha Patel: Regarding accuracy tradeoffs, can you run a shadow accuracy comparison alongside the perf run so we can see exact delta per prompt?
[05:46] Samira Rao: Yes we'll run matched prompt pairs — also capture logits diffs and sample outputs. Expect an S3 link in the results package.
[05:55] Maya Ortiz: There was one odd thing in the traces: a ~400ms spike aligned with garbage collection on one node. Could that be a runtime GC issue?
[06:03] Luca Marin: It could be - some of the older runtimes have periodic housekeeping. We'll instrument the runtime GC and push a build with adaptive GC thresholds.
[06:13] Dr. Neha Patel: Are those kinds of runtime updates part of the pilot deliverables or would they be a separate change?
[06:18] Samira Rao: We can include a candidate runtime tune as part of the pilot. If the spike reproduces, we'll push the adaptive GC for the dedicated slot run.
[06:26] Alex Chen: Quick sanity check on cost math — can someone restate the estimated monthly incremental cost if Oxbridge moves pilot to dedicated for 24/7?
[06:35] Jonas Ek: We haven't decided yet; preliminary numbers in the sheet show dedicated slot at approx $XK/day for the capacity we asked for.
[06:43] Alex Chen: Right, and we model unit cost drop versus hosted because of batching efficiency but reserved monthly commit is needed to get best pricing. We'll include a model in the spreadsheet.
[06:55] Priya Shah: Can Redwood provide an amortized token-cost table per 1M tokens for each routing/batching configuration?
[07:02] Samira Rao: Yes — I'll add per-1M token cost rows for: hosted-latency-first, hosted-cost-first, dedicated-8xbatch-quant8, dedicated-8xbatch-quant6-mixed.
[07:13] Dr. Neha Patel: Going back to the p95 delta, you mentioned a +60ms delta vs our baseline on most slices — is that measured on identical model checkpoints?
[07:21] Samira Rao: Yes, we used the same open-checkpoint you provided. There may be micro differences in kernel placement but model weights are identical.
[07:31] Maya Ortiz: One more data question: are the traces timestamped in UTC? Our observability expects local epoch times.
[07:37] Alex Chen: We'll standardize to UTC epoch and include mapping to your APM spans.
[07:44] Jonas Ek: Concerning security/compliance, we still need the SOC-type docs for the dedicated proposal.
[07:49] Alex Chen: Already on it — I'll share SOC2/ISO artifact links and our private deployment checklist as requested.
[07:56] Priya Shah: Also need encryption at rest details and KMS integration options.
[07:59] Alex Chen: We'll include KMS/HSM options in the doc bundle.
[08:04] Dr. Neha Patel: OK, path forward?
[08:07] Alex Chen: Short: 1) Redwood uploads annotated bench and raw traces (Alex) 2) Redwood runs 2-hr dedicated slot with quant8 and mixed quant6 follow-up (Samira) 3) Oxbridge runs regression on accuracy suite and shares anomalies (Neha) 4) cost modeling and SOC/enc docs (Alex).
[08:30] Maya Ortiz: When will we get the dedicated run results?
[08:33] Samira Rao: Plan to run it by Friday (2027-12-03) and post results same day; if any infra blockers we'll alert earlier.
[08:41] Dr. Neha Patel: Please flag any config differences from the baseline so we can be apples-to-apples.
[08:47] Alex Chen: We'll include a config diff section in the spreadsheet.
[08:52] Priya Shah: Can you also include a copy of the fallback playbook you used that day? We want to understand decision thresholds.
[08:57] Samira Rao: Yes, fallback playbook and thresholds will be included.
[09:02] Alex Chen: Anything else?
[09:05] Jonas Ek: One ask — please indicate which runs had warmed KV cache vs cold start.
[09:09] Samira Rao: Good point, will mark warm vs cold for each run.
[09:14] Dr. Neha Patel: Thanks. That covers it for me.
[09:18] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll share artifacts and follow up on the SE deep-dive invite for Dec 6th.
[09:25] Maya Ortiz: Thanks all.
[09:28] [meeting ends]
